section: Public policy - meaning, types, policy cycle (formulation, implementation, evaluation), policy instruments

accepted.s: Which institution, in association with WRI India, launched the second India Electric Mobility Index?
accepted.x: NITI Aayog, with WRI India, launched the second India Electric Mobility Index.
accepted.tq: Use the institutional-identity approach and distinguish the policy think tank from an evaluation body.

accepted.s: The second India Electric Mobility Index assigns weights to its three major dimensions in which of the following proportions?
accepted.x: The index gives weights of 50:30:20 to transport electrification, charging and research and development, respectively.
accepted.tq: Read the three-part numerical sequence in the same order as the listed dimensions.

accepted.s: The India Electric Mobility Index is intended primarily to reinforce which approach to policymaking?
accepted.x: The index is intended to reinforce evidence-based policymaking by providing an analytical basis for decisions on electric mobility.
accepted.tq: Match the policy instrument with its stated governance purpose rather than with a broad ideological label.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the proposed new retail excise policy in Andhra Pradesh:
1. A Group of Ministers is framing the policy.
2. Kollu Ravindra is the Minister under whose charge the Group of Ministers is functioning.
3. The existing 2024–26 policy expires on 30 September 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: the Group of Ministers is framing the policy under Excise Minister Kollu Ravindra, and the 2024–26 policy expires on 30 September 2026.
accepted.tq: Check the office-holder, institutional arrangement and expiry date separately before selecting the coded combination.

accepted.s: The existing retail excise policy in Andhra Pradesh, for which a new policy is being framed, is scheduled to expire on:
accepted.x: The existing 2024–26 retail excise policy expires on 30 September 2026.
accepted.tq: Use exact-date recall and distinguish the month-end expiry from nearby administrative dates.

accepted.s: The framing of the new retail excise policy in Andhra Pradesh is cited as an example of policy formulation involving:
accepted.x: The policy-framing process is described as a live example of formulation with stakeholder feedback.
accepted.tq: Identify the policy-cycle stage from the action described and connect consultation with formulation.

accepted.s: The shift from announcement-based governance to outcome-based governance is associated with which of the following mechanisms?
accepted.x: The shift toward outcome-based governance is linked with Action Taken Reports (ATRs) and evaluations by the Development Monitoring and Evaluation Office (DMEO).
accepted.tq: Link the governance objective to the monitoring and evaluation mechanisms named with it.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about outcome-based governance:
1. It gives importance to assessing results rather than merely recording announcements.
2. Action Taken Reports are associated with this shift.
3. DMEO evaluations are relevant to this shift.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Outcome-based governance focuses on results and uses ATRs and DMEO evaluations as monitoring and evaluation mechanisms.
accepted.tq: Separate the defining feature from the two supporting mechanisms and test the complete combination.

accepted.s: Andhra Pradesh spent approximately what amount in two years, according to the expenditure figure cited?
accepted.x: The cited expenditure by Andhra Pradesh over two years was ₹2.83 lakh crore.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the overall expenditure figure from the welfare subcomponent mentioned alongside it.

accepted.s: Of the ₹2.83 lakh crore spent by Andhra Pradesh in two years, approximately how much was spent on welfare?
accepted.x: ₹1.49 lakh crore of the total expenditure of ₹2.83 lakh crore was spent on welfare.
accepted.tq: Split the total and component figures instead of treating the larger total as the welfare expenditure.

accepted.s: How much fee reimbursement was provided to SC students in the expenditure period referred to?
accepted.x: Fee reimbursement amounting to ₹1,543.17 crore was provided to SC students.
accepted.tq: Use precise-figure discrimination when two expenditure amounts belong to different categories.

accepted.s: The fee reimbursement of ₹1,543.17 crore in Andhra Pradesh benefited approximately how many SC students?
accepted.x: The fee reimbursement benefited 5.40 lakh SC students.
accepted.tq: Match the exact beneficiary count with the corresponding scheme expenditure figure.

accepted.s: Which one of the following best represents the criticism associated with the idea of “new welfarism”?
o: It eliminates all social protection expenditure
It transfers welfare functions exclusively to local bodies
It strengthens rights-based entitlements in every case
accepted.x: The criticism is that “new welfarism” weakens rights. The cited social protection spending is 4.0% of GDP.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise criticism and reject absolute extensions not supported by the stated position.

accepted.s: Social protection spending, as cited in the discussion of new welfarism, is approximately what percentage of GDP?
accepted.x: Social protection spending is cited as only 4.0% of GDP.
accepted.tq: Focus on the percentage attached to the criticism rather than the separate population-coverage figures.

accepted.s: According to the cited estimate, social protection currently covers approximately what share of the population?
accepted.x: Social protection covers approximately 64.3% of the population.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the current coverage figure from the earlier benchmark of 22%.

accepted.s: Social protection coverage increased from which level in 2016 to 64.3% of the population?
accepted.x: The coverage level increased from 22% in 2016 to 64.3% of the population.
accepted.tq: Read the direction and endpoints of the comparison carefully before selecting the earlier value.

accepted.s: Andhra Pradesh has set which of the following objectives for the year 2047?
o: To become a completely industrialised state
To replace all central welfare schemes
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh aims to become a welfare state by 2047.
accepted.tq: Match the stated long-term target with its exact policy objective and year.
